entry_state: Front wheel off the ground, fork fully extended.
exit_state: Both fork legs back at atmospheric pressure, screws refitted.

required_tools.name: Stand that lifts the front wheel

prerequisites: Do it before every race or practice session: air pressure builds up in the fork as it works and stiffens it.
critical_stop_conditions: Never add air to make the fork stiffer: it is designed to run at atmospheric pressure.
Oil spitting from the screw hole or wet fork tubes: have the seals checked.

steps.title: Record the starting point
steps.instruction: Write down the date and how the fork felt at the end of the last ride. Clean and inspect the fork after each race (or 2.5 hours).

steps.title: Lift the front wheel
steps.instruction: Put a stand under the frame so the front wheel is off the ground and the fork hangs fully extended. Take off the number plate if it is in the way.

steps.title: Open the relief screws
steps.instruction: Remove the pressure relief screw on the top plug of each fork leg and let the trapped air hiss out until the pressure equalises (standard is atmospheric (0 kPa, 0 psi)).

steps.title: Refit the screws
steps.instruction: Refit the screws with their O-rings and tighten them to 1.3 N·m (12 in·lb).

steps.title: Clean the fork tubes
steps.instruction: Wipe mud and dust off the inner tubes so it cannot damage the seals, and look for oil leaks or scratches on the tubes.

steps.title: Record the job
steps.instruction: Note that the air was released and anything you saw on the fork tubes.

entry_state: Bike on a stand, fork clean.
exit_state: Both legs refilled with the same correct amount, fork refitted at standard height, front end torqued, recorded.

required_tools.name: Top-plug wrench to fit the fork

required_parts.name: Fork oil Kawasaki Fork Oil A15-00

prerequisites: Fork cleaned before opening it.
critical_stop_conditions: Unequal oil amounts left and right: do not ride.
Front brake lever not firm: do not ride.

steps.title: Record the starting point
steps.instruction: Change the fork oil every 6 races (or 15 hours). Write down the date, hours and the compression and rebound clicker settings on both legs.

steps.title: Clean the fork
steps.instruction: Wash the fork with mild detergent and plenty of water, without scratching the inner tubes or damaging the dust seals.

steps.title: Support the bike
steps.instruction: Support the bike on a stand under the frame so the front wheel can be lifted off the ground.

steps.title: Loosen the cylinder unit
steps.instruction: Take off the number plate and loosen the upper fork clamp bolts. Cover the cylinder unit with a plastic bag to protect it and loosen it with the top-plug wrench while the fork is still clamped. Do not take it off yet.

steps.title: Take out the front wheel
steps.instruction: Remove the front axle nut and loosen the left axle clamp bolts. Unbolt the brake caliper, rest it on a support so it does not hang on its hose, and put a wooden wedge between the pads. Remove the brake hose clamps and both fork protectors. Loosen the right axle clamp bolts, lift the wheel clear, pull the axle and take off the collars. Do not lay the wheel disc-side down.
verification: Wheel, caliper and guards off, pads wedged.

steps.title: Take out a fork leg
steps.instruction: Loosen the lower fork clamp bolts and pull the leg down out of the clamps, twisting as you go. Do one leg at a time so you can copy its position.

steps.title: Drain the outer tube
steps.instruction: Cover the cylinder unit with a plastic bag, unscrew it from the outer tube with the top-plug wrench and slide the outer tube slowly down. Pour the oil into a drain pan and pump the outer tube several times to push out the rest. Leave the leg upside down until it stops dripping.

steps.title: Check the parts
steps.instruction: Look at the inner tube for scratches and at the oil for metal or water. Wipe the threads clean.

branches.label: Scored tube or dirty oil
branches.condition: Scored inner tube, metal in the oil or milky oil: the fork needs a full rebuild by a suspension specialist. Record it.

steps.title: Refill the outer tube
steps.instruction: With the outer tube slid down, pour 310 mL (10.5 US oz.) of Kawasaki Fork Oil A15-00 into each leg. You can tune it within 305 to 406 mL (10.3 to 13.7 US oz.): more oil makes the end of the stroke firmer, less makes it softer. Both legs must get exactly the same amount.

steps.title: Refit the cylinder unit
steps.instruction: Fit a new O-ring to the cylinder unit if it has one, raise the outer tube and screw the cylinder unit in by hand.

steps.title: Refit the fork leg
steps.instruction: Slide the leg back into the clamps so the top of the upper fork clamp sits 0 mm (0 in.) below the top surface of the fork top plug, the same on both sides. Tighten the lower clamp bolts to 23 N·m (17 ft·lb), going alternately between the two bolts twice. Tighten the cylinder unit to 76 N·m (56 ft·lb) using the top-plug wrench on the torque wrench. Tighten the upper clamp bolts to 23 N·m (17 ft·lb), alternately twice. Repeat for the other leg.
verification: Both legs in at the same height, bolts torqued.

steps.title: Refit the caliper and guards
steps.instruction: Take out the pad wedge and bolt the caliper on at 25 N·m (18 ft·lb). Fit the fork protectors so they do not touch the outer tubes, bolts at 3.5 N·m (31 in·lb), then the brake hose clamps at 7.0 N·m (62 in·lb).

steps.title: Refit the front wheel
steps.instruction: Grease the wheel seals, fit the collars, put the wheel between the legs with the disc between the pads and slide the lightly greased axle in from the right (no grease on the threads). Tighten the axle nut to 80 N·m (59 ft·lb) and the left axle clamp bolts to 23 N·m (17 ft·lb). Loosen the right clamp bolts, pump the fork a few times so the right leg finds its place on the axle, then tighten them to 23 N·m (17 ft·lb), alternately twice.
verification: Wheel in, axle and clamps torqued.

steps.title: Pump the brake
steps.instruction: Pump the front brake lever until it is firm. Never ride before the lever is firm.

steps.title: Reset the clickers
steps.instruction: Set the compression and rebound clickers back to the numbers you wrote down, and release any air with the relief screws.
verification: Clickers back to the recorded settings.

steps.title: Record the job
steps.instruction: Write down the oil used, the amount per leg and the settings.

required_tools.name: Top-plug wrench to fit the fork

required_parts.name: Fork oil Kawasaki Fork Oil A15-00

prerequisites: Fork cleaned before opening it.
critical_stop_conditions: Unequal oil amounts left and right: do not ride.
Front brake lever not firm: do not ride.

steps.title: Record the starting point
steps.instruction: Change the fork oil every 6 races (or 15 hours). Write down the date, hours and the compression and rebound clicker settings on both legs.

steps.title: Clean the fork
steps.instruction: Wash the fork with mild detergent and plenty of water, without scratching the inner tubes or damaging the dust seals.

steps.title: Support the bike
steps.instruction: Support the bike on a stand under the frame so the front wheel can be lifted off the ground.

steps.title: Loosen the cylinder unit
steps.instruction: Take off the number plate and loosen the upper fork clamp bolts. Cover the cylinder unit with a plastic bag to protect it and loosen it with the top-plug wrench while the fork is still clamped. Do not take it off yet.

steps.title: Take out the front wheel
steps.instruction: Remove the front axle nut and loosen the left axle clamp bolts. Unbolt the brake caliper, rest it on a support so it does not hang on its hose, and put a wooden wedge between the pads. Remove the brake hose clamps and both fork protectors. Loosen the right axle clamp bolts, lift the wheel clear, pull the axle and take off the collars. Do not lay the wheel disc-side down.

steps.title: Take out a fork leg
steps.instruction: Loosen the lower fork clamp bolts and pull the leg down out of the clamps, twisting as you go. Do one leg at a time so you can copy its position.

steps.title: Drain the outer tube
steps.instruction: Cover the cylinder unit with a plastic bag, unscrew it from the outer tube with the top-plug wrench and slide the outer tube slowly down. Pour the oil into a drain pan and pump the outer tube several times to push out the rest. Leave the leg upside down until it stops dripping.

steps.title: Check the parts
steps.instruction: Look at the inner tube for scratches and at the oil for metal or water. Wipe the threads clean.

branches.label: Scored tube or dirty oil
branches.condition: Scored inner tube, metal in the oil or milky oil: the fork needs a full rebuild by a suspension specialist. Record it.

steps.title: Refill the outer tube
steps.instruction: With the outer tube slid down, pour 316 mL (10.7 US oz.) of Kawasaki Fork Oil A15-00 into each leg for the standard 4.6 N/mm spring. You can tune it within 310 to 418 mL (10.5 to 14.1 US oz.): more oil makes the end of the stroke firmer, less makes it softer. With the optional soft 4.4 N/mm spring use 323.6 mL (10.9 US oz.) (range 317.6 to 426.5 mL (10.7 to 14.4 US oz.)). With the optional hard 4.8 N/mm spring use 321.2 mL (10.9 US oz.) (range 315.2 to 424.1 mL (10.7 to 14.3 US oz.)). Both legs must get exactly the same amount.

steps.title: Refit the cylinder unit
steps.instruction: Fit a new O-ring to the cylinder unit if it has one, raise the outer tube and screw the cylinder unit in by hand.

steps.title: Refit the fork leg
steps.instruction: Slide the leg back into the clamps so the top of the upper fork clamp sits 5 mm (0.2 in.) below the top surface of the fork top plug, the same on both sides. Tighten the lower clamp bolts to 23 N·m (17 ft·lb), going alternately between the two bolts twice. Tighten the cylinder unit firmly with the top-plug wrench. Tighten the upper clamp bolts to 23 N·m (17 ft·lb), alternately twice. Repeat for the other leg.

steps.title: Refit the caliper and guards
steps.instruction: Take out the pad wedge and bolt the caliper on at 25 N·m (18 ft·lb). Fit the fork protectors so they do not touch the outer tubes, bolts at 3.5 N·m (31 in·lb), then the brake hose clamps at 7.0 N·m (62 in·lb).

steps.title: Refit the front wheel
steps.instruction: Grease the wheel seals, fit the collars, put the wheel between the legs with the disc between the pads and slide the lightly greased axle in from the right (no grease on the threads). Tighten the axle nut to 80 N·m (59 ft·lb) and the left axle clamp bolts to 23 N·m (17 ft·lb). Loosen the right clamp bolts, pump the fork a few times so the right leg finds its place on the axle, then tighten them to 23 N·m (17 ft·lb), alternately twice.
verification: Wheel in, axle and clamps torqued.

title: Set the suspension back to the standard baseline
entry_state: Bike on a stand, suspension clean.
exit_state: Every clicker at standard, preload and fork height checked, pressures set, baseline recorded.
completeness: Covers recording the old settings, setting fork and shock clickers to standard, checking springs, fork height and preload, tyre pressures and a sag reference.
prerequisites: Suspension clean so the adjusters can be counted.
critical_stop_conditions: Never force an adjuster past its seated position: the needle is damaged.
Left and right fork legs set differently: do not ride.

steps.title: Record the current settings
steps.instruction: Before changing anything, count and write down every current setting: turn each adjuster gently clockwise to its fully seated position counting the clicks or turns, then put it back. Also note the rider weight and gear.

steps.title: Confirm the springs
steps.instruction: Check the springs fitted are the standard ones and K = 54 N/mm on the shock. A different spring changes the baseline.

steps.title: Set fork compression
steps.instruction: Compression adjusters are at the top of the fork. Turn each one clockwise until it seats lightly, never forcing it, then back it out 14 clicks counterclockwise (usable range 16 clicks or less from fully seated). Set both legs the same where both have one.

steps.title: Set fork rebound
steps.instruction: Rebound adjusters are at the bottom of the fork. Clean the area, seat each one gently clockwise, then turn it 12 clicks counterclockwise (usable range 16 clicks or less from fully seated).

steps.title: Set shock rebound
steps.instruction: The rebound adjuster is at the bottom of the shock. Seat it gently clockwise, then turn it 12 clicks counterclockwise (usable range 22 clicks or less from fully seated).

steps.title: Set high-speed compression
steps.instruction: On the shock gas reservoir, turn the high-speed compression adjuster (the outer one, turned with a wrench) clockwise until it seats, then out 1 1/4 turns (usable range 4 turns or less from fully seated).

steps.title: Set low-speed compression
steps.instruction: Turn the low-speed compression adjuster (the screwdriver one in the centre) clockwise until it seats, then out 18 clicks (usable range 19 clicks or less from fully seated).

steps.title: Check the fork height
steps.instruction: Check that the top of the upper fork clamp sits 0 mm (0 in.) below the top surface of the fork top plug, the same on both sides. If not, set it while doing the fork oil job.

steps.title: Check the shock preload
steps.instruction: Measure from the centre of the upper shock pivot to the spring preload adjusting nut. Standard is 143.3 mm (5.642 in.).

branches.label: Preload not at standard
branches.condition: Different from standard: set it with the shock preload guide, then come back.

steps.title: Set tyre pressures
steps.instruction: With the tyres cold, set both within 100 to 125 kPa (14 to 18 psi).

steps.title: Measure sag for reference
steps.instruction: With the rider in full gear standing on the pegs, measure how far the rear sinks from fully extended. Write it down as your reference so later spring or preload changes can be compared.

steps.title: Test ride
steps.instruction: Ride a familiar section and note how the bike behaves before making any change. Change one adjuster at a time, in small steps.

steps.title: Record the baseline
steps.instruction: Write down every setting now on the bike, the tyre pressures, the sag and the track conditions.

required_tools.name: Hook wrenches for the shock nuts

prerequisites: Shock spring unloaded before turning the nut.
critical_stop_conditions: Adjusting nut not locked: do not ride.
Outside the adjustable range for the fitted spring: do not ride; fit a different spring instead.

steps.title: Record the starting point
steps.instruction: Write down the current preload nut position, the sag and the date.

steps.title: Take off the rear frame
steps.instruction: This is a long job. Remove the seat, both side covers, the fuel tank and the muffler. Disconnect the battery, negative cable first, and lift it out. Unplug the connectors mounted on the rear frame and open the harness clamps, loosen the air cleaner duct clamp, remove the rear frame bolts on both sides and pull the rear frame rearward together with the airbox. Cover the intake with a clean cloth.
verification: Rear frame off, intake covered, every unplugged connector noted.

steps.title: Lift the rear wheel
steps.instruction: Support the bike so the rear wheel is off the ground and the shock spring is unloaded.

steps.title: Unlock the adjusting nut
steps.instruction: Loosen the spring preload adjusting nut band bolt.

steps.title: Measure the nut position
steps.instruction: Measure from the centre of the upper shock pivot to the adjusting nut. Standard is 143.3 mm (5.642 in.); with the standard K = 54 N/mm spring keep it within 140.8 to 147.8 mm (5.543 to 5.819 in.).

steps.title: Turn the adjusting nut
steps.instruction: Turn the adjusting nut with a hook wrench. Turning it down the shock adds preload; turning it up removes preload. Measure again until you reach the position you want.

steps.title: Lock the nut
steps.instruction: Tighten the band bolt to 5.0 N·m (44 in·lb). Move the spring up and down to be sure it is seated.

steps.title: Refit the rear frame
steps.instruction: Take the cloth out of the intake, refit the rear frame with the airbox and tighten its bolts to 35 N·m (26 ft·lb), then reconnect every connector and clamp, refit the battery positive cable first, and refit the muffler, fuel tank, side covers and seat.
verification: Rear frame back on, intake connected.

steps.title: Check the sag
steps.instruction: With the rider in full gear, check the sag and compare it with your reference.

steps.title: Record the setting
steps.instruction: Write down the new nut position and sag.
